newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks climb to new highs at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks climb to new highs at open.

text.p: Australian shares ventured into record territory at the opening on Tuesday following another record breaking day on Wall Street.
The All Ordinaries index was up 10.8 points at 2,405.5 in early trading after reaching a record high of 2406.3.
Stronger base metals prices further sparked investor enthusiasm, with turnover levels setting sail for the A$300 million level in the first 30 minutes of trade.
"Everyone's in a buying mood so far," said a Sydney broker.
"The Dow keeps going up and turnover looks good. Metals (prices) are also helping the miners," he said.
Macquarie Bank topped turnover early as the Brunei Investment and Commercial Bank bought the 13.4 percent stake held by Hill Samuel, the investment bank unit of Lloyds TSB Plc.
Expectations were for the early gains to hold and perhaps to even be extended in the afternoon. "I think we will hold most of them, we may even go ahead again later," the broker said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 40 percent of stocks traded were steady.
